dedupe_keys.name: low temperature geothermal geospatial data sets an example from alaska

description: This data set compiles baseline geospatial data on low-temperature geothermal resources (below 150 degrees Celsius) in Alaska, to support geothermal heating and cooling, geothermal heat exchange and small-scale low-temperature geothermal power. It was produced at the National Renewable Energy Laboratory by Estefanny Davalos Elizondo, Amanda Kolker and Ian Warren and published on the DOE Geothermal Data Repository, as part of work on bringing geothermal heating and cooling into community energy planning. It gathers information for shallow subsurface ground heat exchange, such as undisturbed ground temperature, and for low-temperature resource availability, including new data from three data sets of isolated geothermal systems and bottom-hole temperatures from oil and gas wells that could be repurposed for co-produced fluids. Coverage is the state of Alaska. Files are a ZIP of six files, about 243 MB, downloadable from the repository (2023) as a publicly accessible submission. Caveats: the licence is not shown in the page text read on the day, and data come from compiled sources of varying density. Simulation uses are screening geothermal heating and cooling potential for community energy planning. Related records: none linked on the provider's pages read on the day.
